items.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Listen to what Jimmy Rowles — listen to Clark Terry from the ‘50s and listen to the latter day Clark Terry and how his style and everything about him at some point in the ‘60s or whenever it was took a quantum leap forward in all respects.

ctx.x: The future’s in some good hands there. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

Oh boy. He’s got a record out, he did “The Man that Got Away.” Ruby plays that too so I’m hoping we’ll play it. It’s [scats] it’s as slow as you can get and swings so hard and he’s just a real force to be reckoned with in this business. You know and I’m listening to him and he’s in his I guess his early, mid-‘30s, I don’t know what his age is. But I was listening to a Jimmy Rowles record from the ‘50s the other day when Jimmy would have been about the age that Bill Charlap is now. And you listen to Bill Charlap…
I really do like listening to him.
